data.risk_justification: mozilla.org is a 1998-registered, registrar- and registry-locked domain held by Mozilla Corporation through MarkMonitor, with DMARC p=reject, SPF present, Google-hosted mail, Akamai DNS, and a clean VirusTotal reputation (0 malicious / 60 harmless). No abandoned or malicious infrastructure appears in passive DNS. The only findings are hardening gaps rather than active threats: DNSSEC is unsigned, SPF ends in ~all with several third-party includes, and 453 CT-visible subdomains include dev/staging/private-named hosts. Wayback data could not be retrieved, but the collected evidence is sufficient to conclude a low risk.
recommendations: Sign the mozilla.org zone with DNSSEC and publish the DS record at the registrar to protect against DNS cache-poisoning and resolver-level tampering.
Tighten SPF: replace the trailing ~all with -all where operationally feasible, and periodically review the third-party includes (vali.email, fundraiseup.com) to remove any no-longer-needed senders.

Inventory the 453 CT-visible subdomains and retire or decommission stale dev/staging hosts (api-dev.bugzilla, api.mig-stage.security, despot-test, apps-preview) or place them behind authentication and non-public DNS.

Monitor Certificate Transparency continuously for new certificates on mozilla.org and its sensitive subdomains (aus*, addons.update, blocklist.addons, *.security) to detect look-alike or unauthorized issuance.
Review the 17 TXT records and remove obsolete third-party verification tokens to reduce the trust surface and stale-provider takeover risk.
Re-run the Wayback Machine (CDX) query later to complete the historical URL and abandoned-subdomain analysis that failed during this run.
Continue enforcing DMARC p=reject with rua/ruf reporting and consider p=reject with stricter subdomain policy (sp=reject) for the whole tree.

## Summary
Passive reconnaissance of mozilla.org (Mozilla Corporation) shows a mature, well-defended domain with strong e-mail authentication and clean reputation; the residual exposure is the very large, partly non-production subdomain footprint visible in public certificate logs.

mozilla.org is a 1998-registered, registrar- and registry-locked domain held by Mozilla Corporation through MarkMonitor, with DMARC p=reject, SPF present, Google-hosted mail, Akamai DNS, and a clean VirusTotal reputation (0 malicious / 60 harmless).
